added_lemmas.statement: Let \(r=(r_0,\ldots,r_{K-1})\) and \(s=(s_0,\ldots,s_{K-1})\) be probability vectors on \(\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), and put \(\Delta_j=\sum_{k=j}^{K-1}(r_k-s_k)\). Among all couplings \((U,V)\) with respective marginals \(r\) and \(s\), the sharp lower and upper bounds on \(P(U>V)\) are \(\max_{0\le j<K}\Delta_j\) and \(1+\min_{0\le j<K}(\Delta_j-r_j)\), respectively.

source.locator: Section 3.1, Proposition 2, equation (6), p. 546; notation for \(\Delta_j\) in equation (1), p. 543
source.verbatim_statement: Proposition 2: The sharp lower and upper bounds of \(\eta\) are \(\eta_L=\max_{0\le j\le J-1}\Delta_j\), \(\eta_U=1+\min_{0\le j\le J-1}(\Delta_j-p_{j+})\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published article PDF at Proposition 2, equation (6), with \(\eta=P\{Y(1)>Y(0)\}\); the emitted lemma only renames the category count and marginal vectors.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(b_L(v)\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen formula has the treatment and control capacity blocks reversed and therefore bounds strict harm, not strict benefit. As an explicit certificate, with \(v^{\ell}\) concentrated at \(K-1\) and \(v^h\) concentrated at \(0\), the frozen formula returns zero although every coupling has benefit probability one. Swapping the two blocks gives the strict-benefit lower capacity and matches Lu--Ding--Dasgupta Proposition 2 when both totals equal one.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(b_U(v)\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen upper-cut formula is oriented toward \(Y(0)>Y(1)\). Swapping the treated and control blocks yields the finite min-cut upper capacity for \(Y(1)>Y(0)\), and is required for coherence with the declared target estimand.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(A^L_r\)

proposed.name: \(A^L_r\)
proposed.def: For each cell, let \(D\) be the diagonal zero-one mask recorded by \(r\). The zero branch contributes \(0\); a cut \(t\) with gap branch \(\gamma\in\{0,1\}\) contributes \(D[(-\mathbf 1\{k\le t\}+\gamma\mathbf 1_K)_{k=0}^{K-1},(\mathbf 1\{k\le t\}-\gamma\mathbf 1_K)_{k=0}^{K-1}]^{\prime}\). Stack these cell vectors over \(x\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This coefficient must be the branch gradient of the corrected \(b_L\). The corrected cut is \(\sum_{k\le t}(v^h_k-v^{\ell}_k)+\gamma(\sum_kv^{\ell}_k-\sum_kv^h_k)\), whose two coefficient blocks are the proposed ones.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(A^U_r\)

proposed.name: \(A^U_r\)
proposed.def: For each cell mask \(D\), an upper cut \(t\) contributes \(D[(\mathbf 1\{k>t\})_{k=0}^{K-1},(\mathbf 1\{k<t\})_{k=0}^{K-1}]^{\prime}\); a mass-cap branch contributes either \(D[(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime},0^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) or \(D[0^{\prime},(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) according to the selected survivor minimum. Stack over \(x\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This coefficient must be the branch gradient of the corrected upper cut \(\sum_{k<t}v^h_k+\sum_{k>t}v^{\ell}_k\). The mass-cap coefficients are unchanged.

proposed.statement: Under perfect compliance, \(D_{ni}(0)=0\) and \(D_{ni}(1)=1\), and universal selection, \(S_{ni}(0)=S_{ni}(1)=1\), one has \(\ell_{n,x,k}=f_{1,n,x,k}\), \(h_{n,x,k}=f_{0,n,x,k}\), \(w_{n,x}=p_{n,x}(f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}\), and \(M_n=1\). Consequently \(\Theta_{I,n}=[\sum_x p_{n,x}b_L((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}),\sum_x p_{n,x}b_U((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime})]\), the covariate-stratified ordinary sharp ordinal-benefit bounds; without covariate stratification these are the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta bounds.
proposed.justification: This reduction checks that the selected-complier capacity formulas collapse to the established ordinal-benefit geometry when compliance and observability cease to be latent.
proposed.gap: Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta establish the ordinary ordinal-benefit bounds; this proposition is a required reduction, not a novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: It gives implementers an exact benchmark for validating the capacity and min-cut code against standard two-arm ordinal data.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the frozen conditional-IV exogeneity, consistency, cell-mass, and instrument-overlap assumptions, and the named Lu--Ding--Dasgupta result. These load-bearing dependencies were missing from the target metadata; the claim text itself is unchanged.
